issues.legal_issue: The burden of disproving undue influence in a gift shifts to its beneficiary only after the donor-beneficiary relationship and the unconscionable nature of the transaction are established.
material_facts: The suit challenged an inter vivos gift made by an elderly donor to his grandson.

The High Court presumed influence from the family relationship and the donor’s age, without finding that the donee was in a position to dominate the donor’s will or that the transaction was unconscionable.
issues.conclusion: The High Court applied the burden of proof in the wrong order. A court must first consider whether the donee was in a position to dominate the donor’s will and whether the transaction was unconscionable; only when both are established does the beneficiary bear the burden of proving that the gift was not induced by undue influence.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 16(1) of the Indian Contract Act, undue influence requires a relationship enabling one party to dominate the other’s will and use of that position to obtain an unfair advantage. Section 16(2) illustrates circumstances in which a person may be in such a position, including real or apparent authority, a fiduciary relationship, or impaired mental capacity. Under section 16(3), where the beneficiary is in a position to dominate the donor’s will and the transaction appears unconscionable, the burden shifts to the beneficiary to prove that the transaction was not induced by undue influence. The same law applies to gifts inter vivos as to contracts. The court applied Raghunath Prasad v. Sarju Prasad, Poosathurai v. Kannappa Chettiar, and Ladli Prasad Jaiswal v. Karnal Distillery Co. Ltd.

predicates.gift_challenged_for_undue_influence: A party to a proceeding challenges a gift on the ground that it was induced by undue influence.
predicates.donee_in_position_to_dominate_donor: The circumstances place the donee in a position to dominate the donor’s will.
predicates.transaction_unconscionable: The transaction appears unconscionable from its terms or the evidence.

issues.definition: When a challenged gift involves a donee able to dominate the donor and an unconscionable transaction, the beneficiary must prove that undue influence did not induce the gift.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of undue influence must be specifically pleaded with particulars of the influence, how it was used, and the unfair advantage obtained.
material_facts: The plaint alleged that the donor was old and mentally impaired, that a relative exercised undue influence, and that the gift was collusive, but the allegations were conflicting and did not clearly set out the alleged domination and its use to obtain an unfair advantage.
The trial issues did not clearly raise undue influence, and the trial court found that the donor understood that he had transferred the property.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings did not sufficiently make out a case of undue influence, so the High Court should not have proceeded to decide the claim on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Before examining whether undue influence was exercised, a court must scrutinise the pleadings for a properly stated case and full particulars, as required for allegations of fraud by Order 6, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. A vague or general plea is insufficient; the pleading must identify the nature of the influence, the manner in which it was used, and the unfair advantage obtained. The court relied on Ladli Prasad Jaiswal v. Karnal Distillery Co. Ltd. and referred to Ismail Mussajeo Mookerdum v. Hafiz Boo.

predicates.undue_influence_claim_in_gift_or_contrac: A party seeks relief in a gift or contract case on the ground of undue influence.
predicates.pleadings_specify_influence_manner_and_u: The pleadings state the precise influence alleged, how it was used, and the unfair advantage obtained.

issues.definition: In a gift or contract case, a claim of undue influence cannot support relief when the pleadings do not specify the alleged influence, its use, and the advantage obtained.

issues.legal_issue: Close family ties, advanced age, or a gift of part of a donor’s property to a grandchild do not, without more, justify presuming undue influence or that the transaction was unconscionable.
material_facts: The donor was about 90 years old when he made the gift to his only grandson.
The donor and donee were closely related, and the gift concerned part of the donor’s property.
The High Court inferred influence from the relationship and age, but did not find that the donee dominated the donor’s will or that the transaction was unconscionable.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s presumptions were unwarranted. Neither close relationship nor the donor’s age alone established undue influence, and the gift to the grandson was not unconscionable merely because of its recipient and timing.
issues.legal_principle: Undue influence requires more than influence arising from a close relationship; the influence must be shown to have been undue. There is no presumption of undue influence merely because donor and donee are closely related, and age alone does not establish imposition or fraud. A gift of part of a donor’s property to a grandchild is not, on that fact alone, unconscionable. The court relied on Poosathurai v. Kannappa Chettiar and Ismail Mussajeo Mookerdum v. Hafiz Boo and referred to the principles stated in Halsbury’s Laws of England.

predicates.undue_influence_claimed: A party challenges a transaction on the ground of undue influence.
predicates.only_basis_is_close_relationship_or_old_: The asserted basis for influence is limited to a close family relationship, the donor’s advanced age, or the fact that the donor gave property to a grandchild.

issues.definition: A claim does not establish presumed undue influence when its only basis is close kinship, advanced age, or a gift to a grandchild.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a donor understood the gift and that the evidence does not establish incapacity or domination cannot be displaced by unsupported presumptions of undue influence.
material_facts: The trial court found that the donor was aware that he had transferred the property and that unsoundness of mind had not been established.
Later property settlements referred to the gift and were witnessed by the donor, and the donor had stated in other proceedings that he had no interest in the property.

The evidence did not establish that the donee dominated the donor’s will, and the High Court reversed the trial court by relying on presumptions based on age, relationship, and the donor’s absence from the family home.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s conclusion was right, the High Court’s approach was unwarranted, and the Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and restored the trial court’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: A donor’s advanced age does not by itself establish unsoundness of mind or undue influence. The burden-shifting rule under section 16(3) of the Indian Contract Act cannot be invoked without the required findings of a position to dominate the donor’s will and an unconscionable transaction. The court relied on Raghunath Prasad v. Sarju Prasad, Poosathurai v. Kannappa Chettiar, and Ismail Mussajeo Mookerdum v. Hafiz Boo.

predicates.appeal_challenges_high_court_reversal_in: An appeal challenges a High Court decision reversing the trial court in a case concerning a gift.
predicates.trial_finding_donor_understood_transfer: The trial court found that the donor understood that the property had been transferred.
predicates.evidence_does_not_establish_incapacity_o: The evidence does not establish that the donor lacked mental capacity or that the donee dominated the donor’s will.
predicates.high_court_relied_on_unsupported_presump: The High Court relied on presumptions that were unsupported by the required findings or evidence.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a High Court reversal in a gift case, the trial court found the donor understood the transfer, the evidence does not establish incapacity or domination, and the reversal rested on unsupported presumptions, the High Court decision is set aside and the trial decision restored.
